Content:
Let's have a look at the diagram below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/442c602e99f0ab84b8e060359f032643]

Content:
The green curve [MATH: y = 3|x|] represents a vertical scaling of [MATH: y = |x|] by a factor of [MATH: 3.] It takes all of the [MATH: y]-coordinates on [MATH: y=|x|] and multiplies them by [MATH: 3.] This has the effect of stretching the curve upwards.

Content:
Now consider the following diagram:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/bb2478e15f0b5d7b1b9e9faf9de852c6]

Content:
The blue curve [MATH: y = \dfrac 1 2 \left |x\right|] is a vertical scaling of [MATH: y = |x|] by a factor of [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}]. It takes all of the [MATH: y]-coordinates on [MATH: y=|x|] and multiplies them by [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}.] This has the effect of squashing, or compressing, the curve downwards.

Content:
In general, the curve [MATH: y = k|x|] is a vertical scaling of the curve [MATH: y=|x|] by a scale factor of [MATH: k] units. If [MATH: k>1] we have stretching, and if [MATH: 0 < k < 1] we have compression (squashing).

sections.normalized_html:
To find the value of [MATH: k,] we can pick a point on the curve [MATH: y=k|x|] and substitute it into the equation.

Notice that the curve passes through the point [MATH: (1,2).] So, we can substitute [MATH: x=1] and [MATH: y=2] into the equation and solve for [MATH: k,] as follows:

[MATH: y|= k|x|; 2|= k ⋅|1|; 2|= k ⋅ 1; 2|= k]

Therefore, [MATH: k =2.]

sections.normalized_html:
To get the graph of [MATH: y=-\dfrac53|x|,] we proceed as follows:

  • Take the graph of [MATH: y=-|x|.]

  • Stretch the graph vertically by a scale factor of [MATH: \dfrac53] to get the graph of [MATH: y=-\dfrac53|x|.]

The result is the solid blue curve, shown above.

Notice that the point [MATH: (3,-5)] lies on the curve because when [MATH: x=3,] we have

[MATH: y|= − (5)/(3) ⋅|3|; = − (5)/(3) ⋅ 3; = − 5.]

items.title: Graphing a Scaled Absolute Value Function Using the Rules of Absolute Value

sections.normalized_html:
First, let's re-write the equation using the rules of absolute value, as follows:

[MATH: y|=|2x|; =|2|⋅|x|; = 2|x|]

Now, to plot the graph of [MATH: y=2|x|,] we proceed as follows:

  • Take the graph of [MATH: y=|x|.]

  • Stretch it vertically by a scale factor of [MATH: 2] to get the graph of [MATH: y=2|x|.]

The result is the solid blue curve, shown below.

Notice that the point [MATH: (1,2)] lies on the curve because when [MATH: x=1,] we have

[MATH: y|=|2 ⋅ 1|; =|2|; = 2.]
